providers.title: Twisted homology in degree zero
providers.scope: For a connected CW complex Z and a nontrivial character rho of its fundamental group, H_0(Z; rho) = 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Euler characteristic with twisted coefficients
providers.scope: For a finite connected complex of dimension at most two and every character rho: dim H_0 - dim H_1 + dim H_2 of the homology twisted by rho is the Euler characteristic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The boundary of a presentation complex by Fox derivatives
providers.scope: For the presentation complex B of <x_1..x_g | r_1..r_h> and a character rho: the boundary C_2(B; rho) -> C_1(B; rho) has the matrix of the Fox derivatives of the relators evaluated at rho, and H_2(B; rho) = 0 exactly if its h rows are linearly independent. Uses the named hypotheses TOP1 to TOP3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Twisted second homology of infinite cyclic covers
providers.scope: For a finite connected complex A of dimension at most two, a character rho and an infinite cyclic cover: if H_2(A; rho) = 0 then the second homology of the cover twisted by the restricted character is 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tower obstruction
providers.scope: Assume the standard theorems TOP1 to TOP6. Let Y be a finite connected CW complex of dimension at most two and rho a character of its fundamental group with H_2(Y; rho) = 0. For every map from a finite connected simplicial complex F with first Betti number 0 to Y, the pullback of rho is trivial.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Characters and elements of finite order
providers.scope: Assume TOP1 to TOP6. If Y is a finite connected CW complex of dimension at most two and H_2(Y; rho) = 0 for a character rho, then rho(g) = 1 for every element g of finite order of the fundamental group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The finite plus construction
providers.scope: Assume TOP1 to TOP4. Let B be a finite connected complex of dimension at most two and K the normal closure of t_1, ..., t_r in P = pi_1(B), with K perfect, G = P/K. Then B is contained in a finite complex X with r more cells of dimension two and r cells of dimension three such that pi_1(X) = G, H_i of the universal cover vanishes for i > 2, H^3(X; M) = 0 for every Z[G]-module M, and H_*(B; N) = H_*(X; N) for every right Z[G]-module N.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A perfect normal subgroup
providers.scope: In the group P = <x_1, a_1, x_2, a_2, s | x_1 a_1 x_1^-1 = a_1^4, x_2 a_2 x_2^-1 = a_2^3, x_1 = a_2^13, s x_2 s^-1 = a_1^5> the normal closure of x_1^2 and x_2^3 is perfect.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The matrix of Fox derivatives of the example
providers.scope: For the character rho(x_1) = -1, rho(a_1) = zeta, rho(x_2) = zeta^2, rho(a_2) = -1, rho(s) = 1 (zeta a primitive cube root of unity) the four rows of Fox derivatives of the relators of P are linearly independent; the minor on the columns x_1, a_1, x_2, s is -4 (1 - zeta^2). So H_2(B; rho) = 0 for the presentation complex B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A counterexample to the finite D(2) problem
providers.scope: Assume the standard theorems TOP1 to TOP6. There is a finite connected CW complex X of dimension three (one vertex, five edges, six two-cells, two three-cells) with H_i of the universal cover 0 for i > 2 and H^3(X; M) = 0 for every module M over the group ring of its fundamental group, that is not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex of dimension at most two.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
